title: Interaction-enabled topological pumping of Rydberg electrons
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, Bryce Gadway
abstract: Topological pumping is a paradigmatic realization of quantized transport in band systems, yet its fate in strongly correlated regimes, especially with long-range interactions, remains largely unexplored. Here we report the experimental observation of interaction-enabled topological pumping of correlated Rydberg electrons in a synthetic lattice. We show that dipolar exchange interactions induce a controllable shift of the underlying topological singularity in parameter space, such that a fixed pumping trajectory can be driven through successive topological transitions by tuning the interaction strength alone. This leads to the emergence and breakdown of quantized transport. The observations are consistent with an effective Rice-Mele description with interaction-renormalized onsite potentials and are supported by characterizing the adiabaticity and robustness to control trajectory imperfections. Our results establish a platform for exploring interaction-controlled topological transport beyond perturbative regimes and open a route toward engineering correlated topological matter in synthetic quantum systems.
summary: The researchers experimentally demonstrated interaction-enabled topological pumping of correlated Rydberg electrons in an optical lattice. They showed that tuning the dipolar exchange interaction strength allows them to controllably shift the system's topological singularity. This control enables the observation and manipulation of quantized transport, opening a pathway for engineering correlated topological matter.
main_problem: Investigating topological pumping in strongly correlated regimes, particularly when long-range dipolar interactions are present.
main_result: The interaction strength can be tuned to shift the underlying topological singularity, enabling and controlling quantized directional transport through successive topological phase transitions.
method: Experimental observation using a two-color microwave driving protocol on Rydberg electrons in a synthetic lattice, analyzed by monitoring state populations over modulation periods.
model_or_system: The system consists of correlated Rydberg electrons trapped in an optical tweezer array. The dynamics are modeled using an effective pair-state Rice-Mele Hamiltonian incorporating dipolar exchange interactions ($V_n \propto 1/d^3$).
key_observables: Pumping efficiency ($\eta$), state populations ($P_n$), and the location of the topological singularity relative to the pumping trajectory.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($V$), modulation frequency ($\omega$), and the ratio of interaction energy to hopping/detuning energies.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to an effective pair-state Hamiltonian and assumes that dipolar exchange interactions are the dominant source of correlation effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the derived effective model (Rice-Mele), the pumping trajectory in parameter space showing singularity shifts, and quantitative measurements comparing correlated vs. uncorrelated transport efficiencies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the unexplored regime (correlated topological pumping) to deriving an effective Hamiltonian via gauge transformations, demonstrating how interaction strength controls the topology, and finally presenting experimental evidence of quantized transport breakdown/emergence based on this control.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges concepts from condensed matter topology (topological pumping) with state-of-the-art AMO platforms (Rydberg atoms), providing a clean, controllable system to study interaction effects beyond simple mean-field approximations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Experimental scheme for interaction-enabled topological pumping of correlated Rydberg electrons. (a) An array of independent pairs of two Rydberg atoms prepared with optical tweezers (A and B) with tunable separation d are driven by multi-frequency microwave fields, forming a synthetic lattice of Rydberg states |n⟩. Each nearest-neighbor transition is coupled by two microwave tones with time-dependent amplitudes J±(t) and phases θ±(t). Dipolar exchange interactions scale as Vn ≈V ∝1/d3. (b) Effective Rice-Mele representation in the pair basis |an⟩= |n⟩A ⊗|n⟩B = |n, n⟩ and |bn⟩= |+⟩n = (|n⟩A ⊗|n + 1⟩B + |n + 1⟩A ⊗|n⟩B)/ √

FIG. 2. Pumping dynamics for Rydberg electrons in synthetic lattices. Measured population Pn in each of the synthetic sites |n⟩over one modulation period for (a) corre- lated pairs with V = ∆c and (b) uncorrelated singles with V = 0. The pumping parameters used are: ∆c/h = 3.0 MHz, ∆/h = 2.4 MHz, J0/h = 0.3 MHz, and ω/2π = 0.3 MHz. The solid lines in each panel are numerical simulation results with the original Hamiltonian (1), by taking into account the initial state preparation inefficiency. The dashed lines in (a) indicate simulation results by assuming perfect initial state preparation. The error bars are standard errors from multi- ple independent experimental data sets.

FIG. 3. Adiabaticity of the interaction-enabled topo- logical pumping. Measured population P0,0(t = π/ω) in the initial |a0⟩= |0, 0⟩state as a function of the modulating fre- quency ω. The pumping parameters used are: V/h = ∆c/h = 3.0 MHz, ∆/h = 2.4 MHz, and J0/h = 0.3 MHz. The solid light and dark lines are numerical simulation results with and without the consideration of the initial state preparation in- efficiency, respectively. The dashed vertical lines indicate the positions of critical values of ω derived from the Landau-Zener (LZ) adiabatic conditions [52]. The error bars are standard errors from multiple independent experimental data sets.
